title: Your First Weekend at California State Polytechnic University-Pomona, Shared as Cards
description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning the campus layout, finding distinctive outdoor spaces, eating on campus, and encountering CPP’s agricultural heritage.

cards.title: Start With the Campus Map
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · establish your bearings
cards.notes: Open the interactive campus map before walking, then identify Building 1, the CLA complex, housing, and your return route.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a map-based orientation instead of wandering between CPP’s widely separated campus areas.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP’s visitor-information page provides links for the campus map, directions, parking, dining, shopping, tours, and ADA assistance.
cards.source_title: Visit Cal Poly Pomona: Campus Tours, Maps, and More
cards.access_notes: Review parking rules before arriving; visitor tour parking requires registration and a designated tour space.

cards.title: See Where Student Projects Begin
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · hands-on campus preview
cards.notes: Stop in during walk-in hours, inspect the fabrication resources, and note where to return when a class or club project takes shape.
cards.short_summary: The iLab introduces CPP’s student-facing prototyping culture in a concrete, approachable setting.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP identifies the iLab in Building 1, Room 113 as a collaboration and fabrication space with weekday walk-in hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open walk-in Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; plan this stop for Friday and verify exceptions before going.

cards.title: Use the CLA Paseo as a Landmark
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · practice campus wayfinding
cards.notes: Walk through the upper paseo, study the distinctive architecture, and use the surrounding paths to rehearse navigation across campus.
cards.short_summary: A pass through the CLA Paseo turns one of CPP’s defining structures into a practical wayfinding reference.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP’s campus map identifies the CLA Paseo as the paseo portion of Building 98 and describes the CLA Building as a defining image of the university.
cards.access_notes: The map page identifies the location but does not publish general access hours; remain in publicly accessible outdoor areas.

cards.entity_name: George and Sakaye Aratani Japanese Garden
cards.title: Slow Down at the Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · quiet outdoor reset
cards.notes: Follow the walkways past the pond, bridges, and waterfall, keeping pathways clear and leaving planted and rock areas undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: This compact garden offers a defined pause between the academic core and the rest of the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP describes the 1.3-acre George and Sakaye Aratani Japanese Garden as containing traditional Asian flora, a pond, waterfall, bridges, walkways, and an amphitheater.
cards.access_notes: No public hours are stated on the cited page; visit only when campus access and posted conditions permit.

cards.title: Connect the Garden Landmarks
cards.subtitle: Friday early evening · finish the core-campus loop
cards.notes: Walk north from the Japanese Garden, locate the Rose Garden on the official map, and save the route for future campus crossings.
cards.short_summary: Linking the two named gardens creates an easy mental map of CPP’s central outdoor spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP’s official campus map places the Rose Garden north of the Japanese Garden and northeast of Engineering Laboratories, Building 17.
cards.access_notes: The map provides location information but no general visiting hours; follow campus signs and any event closures.

cards.title: Make Dinner a Campus Logistics Test
cards.subtitle: Friday dinner · learn the dining routine
cards.notes: Check the live schedule and payment options first, then use the meal to learn Building 72 and its relationship to the residences.
cards.short_summary: A first meal at Centerpointe doubles as an introduction to CPP’s primary residential dining area.
cards.evidence_claim: CPPE Dining identifies Centerpointe in Building 72 as an all-you-care-to-eat dining commons serving students, faculty, staff, and the public.
cards.access_notes: Meal periods vary by day and academic calendar; consult the live Centerpointe page immediately before visiting.

cards.title: Walk Through CPP’s Living Collections
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · self-guided outdoor learning
cards.notes: Explore the outdoor learning areas at an unhurried pace, yield to scheduled groups, and enter the rainforest only if its doors are open.
cards.short_summary: BioTrek turns a Saturday walk into an introduction to CPP’s rainforest, native-plant, and Mesozoic collections.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP states that BioTrek’s outdoor spaces are open to the public for self-guided visits and that visitors may enter the rainforest when the glasshouse doors are open.
cards.source_title: Planning Your Visit – Rain Bird BioTrek
cards.access_notes: Outdoor spaces allow self-guided public visits; scheduled tours have priority, and rainforest entry depends on open glasshouse doors.

cards.entity_name: Cal Poly Pomona Farm Store at Kellogg Ranch
cards.title: Trace Campus Agriculture to the Farm Store
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · see CPP-grown products
cards.notes: Browse the produce, nursery, and campus-made goods, then note how AGRIscapes connects agricultural instruction with a public storefront.
cards.short_summary: The Farm Store makes CPP’s agricultural production visible beyond classrooms and research plots.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP lists the Farm Store at 4102 South University Drive and states that it is open daily from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., subject to listed holiday closures.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; closed on the holidays enumerated by the Farm Store. Purchases are optional but cost money.

cards.entity_name: CPP Metal Letters at Park at 98
cards.title: Take a First-Weekend Photo at Park at 98
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · mark the end of day two
cards.notes: Frame a quick group photo at the metal CPP letters, keep circulation routes open, and use Building 98 to recheck your bearings.
cards.short_summary: The freestanding CPP letters provide a specific, recognizable endpoint for Saturday’s campus loop.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP News identifies the metal CPP letters at Park at 98, in front of Building 98, as an installed campus photo location.
cards.source_title: Where to Take Graduation Pictures on Campus
cards.access_notes: The source provides no visiting hours; photograph only from an open public area without blocking paths or scheduled activity.

cards.entity_name: W.K. Kellogg Arabian Horse Center Sunday Show
cards.title: Close With a School-Specific Tradition
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · conditional heritage stop
cards.notes: Check the show schedule and weather notice before leaving, arrive with time to find the outdoor arena, and leave pets at home.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled Sunday Show connects the weekend to the Arabian-horse program that helped shape CPP’s identity.
cards.evidence_claim: CPP documents the Sunday Show as a tradition begun by W.K. Kellogg in 1926, featuring student riders and Arabian horses on scheduled first Sundays at 2 p.m., weather permitting.
cards.access_notes: Conditional stop: shows are scheduled for first Sundays at 2 p.m., weather permitting. Check the current schedule; pets other than service animals are prohibited.
